title: Quantum models with the Yang-Lee phase transition
abstract: In this article, we present four different $1+1$D quantum models that realize the Yang-Lee (YL) phase transition under a deformation that preserves $PT$ symmetry. These are the antiferromagnetic Ising spin chain in transverse and longitudinal magnetic fields, the massive Schwinger model, the Blume-Capel model, and the three-state quantum clock model. Using the state-operator correspondence, we identify the YL critical point, compute the scaling dimensions of the lowest operators in each model, and find perfect agreement with the exact results for the YL criticality in two dimensions. Using bosonization for the Schwinger model and the Polyakov-Hubbard transformation for the other models, we show that in all of these quantum models the YL critical point is described, as expected, by a massless bosonic field with an $i φ^3$ interaction. In the quantum clock model, this critical field interacts with a massive bosonic field, and we identify the massless and massive states in the Hamiltonian spectrum. In addition, we numerically compute the two-point function of $φ$ at the Yang-Lee critical point and show that it grows with distance, in agreement with theoretical expectations.
summary: This paper analyzes four distinct 1+1D quantum models—including Ising, Schwinger, Blume-Capel, and clock models—to study the Yang-Lee phase transition. Using advanced field-theoretic methods, the authors demonstrate that these diverse physical systems all map onto a universal critical theory described by an i\phi^3 massless bosonic field. This confirms deep connections between symmetry protection, quantum criticality, and conformal field theory.
main_problem: The research investigates quantum models that exhibit the Yang-Lee (YL) phase transition under deformations that preserve PT symmetry.
main_result: In all four studied quantum models, the YL criticality is consistently described by a massless Euclidean i\phi^3 field theory in the continuum limit.
method: The authors employ advanced theoretical techniques including state-operator correspondence, bosonization, and the Polyakov-Hubbard transformation to map microscopic Hamiltonians onto effective bosonic field theories.
model_or_system: Four specific 1+1D quantum models are analyzed: the antiferromagnetic Ising spin chain (with transverse/longitudinal fields), the massive Schwinger model, the Blume-Capel model, and the three-state quantum clock model. These systems are deformed to induce YL criticality.
key_observables: Scaling dimensions ($\Delta$), effective central charge ($c_{	ext{eff}}$), two-point correlation functions $\langle \phi(0)\phi(n) angle$, and pseudo-critical points ($h^*$).
important_parameters: The dimensionality $1+1$D, the imaginary coupling constant (related to the YL singularity), and system size $N$.
main_assumptions: Approximations include using the state-operator correspondence and assuming that low-energy physics is governed by an effective continuum field theory description.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams, spectral flow showing crossings between different critical points (Ising vs. YL), and numerical results for correlation functions comparing theoretical power laws to exponential decays.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes multiple models, deriving effective LGW actions via transformations, calculating scaling dimensions using finite-size scaling on the low-energy spectrum, and confirming the underlying CFT description of the critical point.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection drawn between diverse physical lattice models (Ising, clock) and a single universal critical theory ($i\phi^3$ CFT) provides powerful insights into how symmetry constraints dictate quantum criticality in condensed matter systems.
